title: Lenses and image formation
target: Use ray directions to explain converging and diverging lens behavior.
criteria: Trace principal rays with a clear optical axis.
State whether an image is real or virtual in the given case.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: An ideal thin lens bends parallel rays toward a common point on the far side. What type is it?
cpa.guide: Converging lenses bring initially parallel rays toward a focus.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Parallel rays spread after passing through an ideal thin lens and appear to come from a near-side focus. What type is it?
cpa.guide: A diverging lens makes parallel rays spread as though emitted from its near focus.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: For a converging lens, a ray initially parallel to the optical axis refracts along which path?
options: Through the lens center regardless of its entry height.
cpa.guide: This is a principal ray rule for an ideal thin converging lens.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: In the ideal thin-lens model, how is a ray through the optical center usually drawn?
options: Straight through without significant angular deflection.
Along the axis even if it entered at an angle.
cpa.guide: The optical-center principal ray is drawn approximately undeviated.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A real object is placed beyond twice the focal length of a converging lens. Which image type is predicted?
options: Real and inverted, between f and 2f on the far side.
Virtual and upright on the object side.
cpa.guide: Principal rays intersect on the far side between f and 2f, giving a real inverted image.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A magnifying glass is used with the object closer to the lens than its focal length. Which image is predicted by the ideal converging-lens model?
options: Upright and virtual on the object side.
Inverted and real on a screen beyond the lens.
cpa.guide: Refracted rays diverge; backward extensions meet on the object side in a virtual enlarged image.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.
